source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Cooling, p.6K-3

procedures.title: Thermostat: replace and test
steps: Remove the housing bolts and take off the water outlet and gasket (see figure 2 in the manual).
Put the thermostat fully under water 25° hotter than the temperature stamped on the valve and stir well; it should open fully.
Move it to water 10° below the stamped temperature, fully submerged and stirred; it should close completely.
If it passes, refit it with a new housing gasket.
notes: The thermostat sits in the housing at the cylinder head water outlet above the water pump.

procedures.title: Water pump: remove and install
steps: Drain the radiator and break the fan pulley bolts loose.
Disconnect the heater hose, lower radiator hose and bypass hose at the pump as needed.
Loosen the Delcotron, take off the fan belt, then remove the fan bolts, fan and pulley.
Remove the pump-to-block bolts and take off the pump and old gasket.
Installation: fit the pump to the block with a new sealer-coated gasket and tighten the bolts securely.

Fit the pulley and fan on the pump hub and tighten securely; a 5/16"-24 x 1-1/2" bolt with its head cut off, screwed into one hub hole as a guide stud, helps line up hub, pulley and fan; remove it after starting the other 3 bolts.
Connect the hoses and refill the cooling system.
Install and adjust the fan belt.
Start the engine and check for leaks.
notes: Keep a thermostatic fan clutch in its in-car attitude; off the car, support it so the clutch disc stays vertical to stop silicone fluid leaking.
